item.title: Version 1.4.0
item.description:
2026-08-02 - Version 1.4.0, the Round Trip series (PRs #144-#148)

New Features

  • Word documents convert back to Markdown. Drop a .docx on the panel’s new To Markdown target, the tray icon, or the Dock icon, and clean GitHub-flavored Markdown lands in a folder you choose once. Embedded images come out into an images folder beside the document. Handy for the round trip AI work creates: a client sends a Word doc, and you want its text in Claude or ChatGPT without retyping anything.
  • Sections choose their own formatting. The switches on the Advanced tab stay the defaults, and any section can carry its own set instead: a client report gets a table of contents and numbered headings, meeting notes get neither. Every entry point honors the override, from drops to watched folders to the integrations.
  • Watched folders decide what happens to the source file. After a successful conversion the Markdown can stay put, move to a Processed folder, or go to the Trash, per section. Failures always stay to be fixed and retried, and nothing is ever hard-deleted.
  • A quiet What’s New note appears once on the first launch after an update, since automatic installs skip the update window and its release notes. Fresh installs skip the note; everything is new there anyway.

Fixes

  • The section editor outgrew the screen once sections learned this many tricks; it now grows sideways instead. Two columns, with folder watching and per-section formatting each behind a switch, so the simple case stays simple and Save stays reachable.
  • Captions in Settings and the section editor wrap instead of clipping mid-sentence. Ships as 1.4.0 (build 10).

item.title: Version 1.3.1
item.description:
2026-08-01 - Version 1.3.1, pandoc 3.10.1 and a pinned version (PR #134)

  • The bundled pandoc is now 3.10.1, picking up upstream’s latest round of small fixes (#133). The fetch script pins the exact version it installs instead of grabbing whatever is newest, so the repo records what every build bundles and a pandoc update becomes a deliberate one-line change. The script still verifies the maintainer’s Developer ID signature and notarization, and now also confirms the installed binary matches the pinned version. Ships as 1.3.1 (build 9).

item.title: Version 1.3.0
item.description:
2026-08-01 - Version 1.3.0, the app updates itself (PR #127)

  • Check for Updates lives in the tray menu, and the app checks quietly once a week on its own (#62). When a new version exists, a window shows what changed and one click installs it, verified against the app’s signing key before a byte of it runs. Two switches in General tune the behavior: the weekly check itself, and fully automatic installs for people who never want to think about versions. No internet? Nothing appears; a background check that fails just waits for next week. Downloads and the update feed live in the public releases repo, so the code can stay private while updates flow. This is 1.3.0 (build 8), the first build that can update itself: anyone on 1.2.1 grabs the new DMG once, and never again.
